Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> Football Profligate Hearts punished in 2-2 draw with Aduana Source : Victor Atsu Tamakloe 22 November 2026 5:43pm ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
Accra Hearts of Oak surrendered a two-goal lead to settle for a 2-2 draw with Aduana F.C. in the Ghana Premier League on Sunday.
Hearts went into the game chasing top spot and got a deserved start after thirteen minutes.
The Phobians took the lead when Hussein Mohammed's fine, left foot strike from the inside the box found the bottom corner.
Five minutes after restart, Hearts consolidated their lead when Seidu Saana turned Henry Kwaku Boateng's cross into his own net.
The midfielder had slid in ostensibly to block Hussein Mohammed from scoring a second, only to divert the ball in to his own net.
Aduana fought to get back into the game but struggled to find a way past the Hearts defence.
Eight minutes from full time, however, Stephen Amankona produced a fine volley to reduce the deficit.
Moments later, a mistake allowed Hearts striker Frank Duku to have a free run at goal, but the Hearts striker fired wide.
Two minutes into stoppage time, Hearts were punished for their profligacy when Alex Boakye scored on the half-volley from a corner to level the game.
Sunday's draw means Hearts missed the opportunity to go top of the league and are now third on 22 points, behind Bechem United and Medeama SC who have a game in hand and on 24 points.
